comments.text:
Needhelp5565
★ PBH101, SBAH
she teaches well and her lectures are very straightforward and short. just studying slides are enough to do good. she marks the important topics during lectures so be attentive during class.
questions come directly from slides and she prefers answers that are straight to the point.
super lenient grading, gives bonus marks/curves.
she takes 2 quizzes (both counted), 1 mid, 1 assignment and 1 group poster presentation. she takes make up quiz and mid as well.
★ HRM360, ALM
TEACHING: Alima ma'am teaches well however she speaks a bit fast and her slides don't have all the detailed info so it's VERY IMPORTANT to be attentive in class and take proper notes. she's very open to answering questions and will explain the same thing again and again if needed. there are a few maths in the course including ratio & trend analysis, regression analysis and markov analysis which she explains in a very easy to grasp manner and also makes you practice in class to ensure that students actually understood it.
GRADING: fair grading. her questions are mostly conceptual, the MCQs may be a bit tricky or confusing but her questions always come from the class lectures, so if you attend the classes regularly you can get good marks. for Q/A she doesn't give suggestions but you can catch what's important by analyzing the amount of time she spends explaining the topic. questions come from topics that she puts more time into making sure that you understand. there's 3 quizzes, 1 mid, 2 case studies, 1 group report, 1 presentation and final alongside these she also takes surprise pop quizzes.
- Question Pattern:
QUIZ: only MCQs.
MID: MCQs, 1 Q/A & 1 mini case study Q/A
FINAL: MCQs, one long math, 2 short Q/A.
- REPORT/PRESENTATION: on HR Planning Process of a hypothetical organization.
EXTRA:
- she's very approachable and sweet however it's important to maintain punctuality as she doesn't like it AT ALL when people constantly come late to class.
- do participate in class, ask questions and try to answer her questions as well.
- always go through the previous lectures as she might take pop quizzes.
- she's very open to answering questions and solving doubts during class as well as her office hours, not just for her course, you can also discuss any other academic issues or queries with her, she's always happy to help her students out.
- it's a major course and she treats it like that so it's best not to go in thinking it'll be like 200-level courses with definition-based questions or questions directly from slides, you actually need to study and put effort to get a good grade under her.
